Golden file for :domain:engines:loan (issue 6.2; FR-ACC-003, MNY-001/MNY-002, P-08).

Every block is one loan and its ENTIRE amortisation schedule, instalment by instalment. Amounts are
PAISE (MNY-001), never rupees - a fixture written in rupees is a fixture that silently passes at a
hundredth of the amount it claims. The rate is integer BASIS POINTS (MNY-002): 850 is 8.5%, not 850%.

Why the whole schedule and not a few sampled rows: the two invariants this issue exists to hold are
about the schedule as a WHOLE - the principals sum to the loan, and the closing balance reaches
exactly zero. Those are properties of the last row given all 239 before it, and a fixture that
sampled rows 1, 120 and 240 would pass while every row in between drifted. `LoanEnginePropertyTest`
proves the invariants over generated terms; this file proves the exact paise for terms a person can
check against their own bank statement.

The expected figures were produced by an INDEPENDENT implementation of the same formula (a
50-significant-digit decimal script), not by capturing this engine's own output. A golden file
regenerated from the code it guards asserts only that the code has not changed, which is not the
same thing as asserting it is right.

Block format - a `# key=value` header block, then one pipe-separated row per instalment, blocks
separated by a line of `===`:

  label            what this loan is, so a failure names the case
  principal        paise, the sanctioned amount
  rate_bps         annual rate in integer basis points; 0 is a real 0% EMI
  tenure           the number of instalments the loan was sanctioned for
  first_emi        ISO yyyy-MM-dd, when the first instalment falls (TIM-002)
  emi_override     paise, the instalment the lender actually charges; `-` to derive it
  expect_emi       paise, the instalment the schedule is built from
  expect_basis     DERIVED or LENDER_STATED
  expect_rows      how many instalments the loan actually takes - LESS than `tenure` when an
                   override clears it early
  expect_interest  paise, the total interest over the life of the loan

  row: number|due_iso_date|amount|principal|interest|closing_balance
